title: IaC Preflight Operator: Comprehensive pre-install checks for Private VPC installs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement an IaC-friendly 'preflight operator' and Terraform validation modules that run before Private (VPC) installs. The goal is to catch common installation failures early by verifying cloud quotas, IAM permissions, DNS delegation and records, VPC/subnet capacity, GPU instance availability, and KMS/bucket configuration. The operator should be usable as a Terraform null_resource provisioner step, a CLI check (redwood preflight --target private), and an optional Kubernetes job run inside customer clusters for live health checks.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Cloud quota checks (vCPU, ENIs, EBS), GPU instance availability and quotas, required IAM roles/policies, DNS delegation + private hosted zone accessibility, required subnet IP capacity and AZ distribution, KMS key accessibility and key policies, S3/GCS bucket access, and expected service endpoints. Produce a machine-readable preflight report (JSON) with per-check severity and remediation hints. Integrate with existing Terraform modules so that the check can be injected as a pre-apply gate.
- Non-goals: Full remediation automation (we will surface fixes, but not auto-modify customer infra), inventorying third-party vendor quotas beyond major clouds, or replacing cloud provider console checks for edge cases.

Design decisions (high level):
1) Two components: (A) Terraform validation module (redwood_preflight) implemented as Terraform module + external data source script that calls cloud SDKs; (B) Preflight operator binary (Go) used by customers who prefer a CLI or Kubernetes Job. Both produce the same JSON schema for results.
2) Use cloud provider SDKs (AWS/Azure/GCP) directly from the external check to avoid fragile CLI parsing. For Terraform/CDK users we provide a lightweight wrapper that invokes the check and writes state to an S3/GCS blob.
3) Checks are idempotent and time-bounded (per-check timeout default 60s, configurable). Failures are classified as hard-fail (block install) or advisory. Defaults: quota shortfall for requested GPU fleet = hard-fail, missing IAM permissions for provisioner = hard-fail, missing private hosted zone delegation = hard-fail, transient API errors = advisory + retry.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module redwood_preflight can be added as a pre-apply gate and will return non-zero exit when any hard-fail check fails.
- CLI 'redwood preflight --plan <tfplan> --cloud aws|gcp|azure' outputs JSON report and human-readable summary, exit code 0 only when no hard-fail checks.
- Operator binary provides detailed remediation hints and links to internal runbooks/Confluence pages.
- Integration tests for AWS: simulate quota limits (using quota API mocks), test missing IAM policies, validate private hosted zone detection.
- Documented sample Terraform usage in Confluence and a reference GitHub repo with examples.

Risks / mitigations:
- Risk: Cloud provider API rate limits while scanning many quotas. Mitigation: backoff and per-account caching; provide throttle options.
- Risk: False negatives for cross-account role assumptions. Mitigation: support assume-role ARN override and explicit test credentials.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module sources + README (module variables, outputs, examples)
- Go preflight operator CLI + Docker image + k8s Job manifest example
- JSON schema for preflight report and converter for Console upload
- Integration test harness and CI job (uses recorded HTTP fixtures for provider SDKs)
